 MESSAGE FROM THE UEFA PRESIDENT

UNITY. ACTION. IMPACT.

Dear friends,

European football has always been more 
than the game itself. It reflects the world 
around the game, connects communities 
and cultures within and across borders. 

Today, that role carries an added 
expectation: to respond meaningfully 
and decisively to the growing challenges 
in human rights and the environment. 
These issues are no longer peripheral 
to football, but a significant factor in 
how our competitions are organised and 
experienced. 

They demonstrated that global sporting 
events can raise standards in this 
delicate, fast-evolving field, and they 
reinforced a clear message: football 
can lead by example. At the same time, 
expectations continue to rise - from 
societies, member associations, clubs, 
leagues, fan groups, players, host 
communities and partners.

That is why we are updating our 
sustainability strategy: to reflect new 
trends, strengthen our approach, 
and ensure our commitments remain 
relevant, robust and measurable. 

We can be proud of the progress made 
to date. Sustainability is increasingly 
embedded in how UEFA works and in 
how we deliver our major tournaments. 
In particular, UEFA EURO 2024 and 
UEFA Women’s EURO 2025 marked 
significant milestones. 

Our direction is clear. Football has an 
unmatched ability to mobilise people, 
amplify messages and accelerate 
change. With one of the largest 
communities in Europe, we have both an 
opportunity and a responsibility to use 
that reach for lasting positive impact.

That is the essence of the Strength 
through Unity Strategy. Real progress 
on complex social and environmental 
challenges can only be achieved when 
we work together, align on priorities, 
listen to each other, and act consistently 
across the football ecosystem. UEFA will 
continue to set the standard through 
strong policies, clear targets and KPIs, 
and a long-term perspective.

Until 2030, we will continue to build on 
the foundation of unity and solidarity 
that defines European football, deepen 
cooperation with stakeholders, and 
strengthen partnerships at the European 
and global level. Our goal is practical 
and ambitious: to protect the people 
who make football possible, reduce our 
environmental footprint, and help ensure 
that the game remains a positive force 
for society. 

As I said back in 2022, when this 
strategy was launched - only by acting 
together can we unlock the full power 
of football and inspire millions to drive 
sustainable change, on and  
beyond the pitch.

Aleksander Čeferin 
UEFA President

 FOREWORD: EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR SOCIAL & 
ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY

IMPACT BEYOND THE GAME

Football is one of Europe’s most 
powerful social infrastructures. Its 
reach, trust, and cultural relevance 
position it not only as a sport, but as a 
scalable platform capable of generating 
measurable social value while reinforcing 
long-term institutional strength. 

For UEFA, impact is not peripheral. It is a 
core value driver.

WHY WE ARE UPGRADING  
OUR STRATEGY IN 2025
Our initial strategy Strength Through 
Unity in 2021 established the 
foundations and the journey: a unified 

framework and a common language 
linking football to responsibility, 
credibility, concreteness, and long-term 
value creation. In 2025, we entered 
an upgrade phase—reflecting a more 
mature ecosystem and anticipating 
societal expectations. Sustainability, 
once exploratory, is now assumed. 

What distinguishes leadership today 
is no longer intent, but the ability to 
deliver results at scale. Across European 
football, standards have strengthened, 
guidelines and data systems have 
developed, and stakeholder alignment 
has increased. 

The football ecosystem is ready to 
move beyond commitments toward 
outcomes—measured, comparable, and 
credible.

FROM SUSTAINABILITY 
TO IMPACT PERFORMANCE 
The language of sustainability, on its 
own, is no longer sufficient. 

Our focus now is impact performance: 
what football tangibly delivers to society, 
and how effectively it deploys its social 
capital. 

Our impact thesis is anchored in three 
pillars: 

 - System integrity: safeguarding trust, 
fairness, and credibility across the 
game 

 - Targeted capital allocation: investing 
where football can generate the 
highest social return 

 - Contextual relevance: respecting 
cultural diversity while applying 
shared standards  

We prioritise interventions with clear 
pathways from input to outcome, 
favouring execution over narrative, 
evidence over intention, and partnership 
over soloist. 

BEYOND 2030: 
LONG-TERM VALUE CREATION 
While 2030 remains a useful reference 
point, meaningful impact requires a 
longer horizon. Football operates across 
social and cultural cycles measured 
in generations. Our responsibility is to 
ensure that today’s decisions enhance 
future optionality—strengthening 
institutions, reducing systemic risk, 
and preserving relevance over time. 
Impact, in this sense, is not a short-term 
programme but a long-term investment 
in resilience, credibility, and continuity.

 EXECUTION, MEASUREMENT, 
AND CREDIBILITY 
Impact without a clear strategy, an 
action plan and measurement of 
indicators remains aspiration. 

THE DOUBLE RETURN: 
RETURN OF INVESTMENT  
PLUS RISK OF INACTION  
Our approach delivers a clear  
dual return: 

Our framework is designed for 
continuous assessment — tracking 
progress, stress-testing assumptions, 
and adapting where evidence 
demands it. 

For the first time, our Respect Report for 
the 2024/25 season has been developed 
in line with an international standard 
and independently assured by a third 
party. This marks a decisive shift away 
from symbolic compliance toward 
verifiable impact—responding directly to 
growing scrutiny around greenwashing 
and social-washing claims. 

 - Positive impact and long-term  
value creation through action 

 - Risk mitigation through  

anticipation rather than reaction  

Inaction compounds risk—reputational, 
regulatory, and financial. 

For football institutions, proactive 
impact investment is not only  
value-enhancing; it is a form of 
anticipatory leadership—the capacity to 
identify social and environmental trends 
early, adapt ahead of pressure, and 
shape change rather than absorb it. 

Credibility is built through transparency, 
discipline, persistence, and consistency 
over time.

This is leadership defined not by 
response, but by foresight.

SCALING IMPACT: 
FROM INSTITUTIONAL  
TO COMMUNITY CAPITAL 
The next phase of football’s contribution 
to concrete social and environmental 
impact requires a structural shift. 

A PLATFORM FOR COLLECTIVE 
ENGAGEMENT AND LEADERSHIP
This evolution reflects a broader 
ambition: positioning football as a 
credible and proactive partner within  
the impact investment ecosystem. 

After five years of largely top-down 
momentum, progress must now 
extend bottom-up — where thanks to 
the synergy with our stakeholders, 
grassroots football, fans and 
communities become active contributors 
to outcomes, not only passive 
beneficiaries. 

Institutions play a catalytic role: setting 
standards, enabling capital flows, and 
amplifying proven solutions.

Here, football’s distributed network 
becomes a strategic advantage — 
allowing impact to scale through 
proximity, trust, and participation. 

By aligning governance, capital, and 
community action, football evolves 
from a sport asset into a long-term 
impact platform—capable of delivering 
measurable outcomes while reinforcing 
the values that underpin the game. 

Football’s greatest return is not only 
what it wins or transmits on the pitch, 
but what it builds for society over time. 

By upgrading the strategy, UEFA 
reinforces its focus on execution, 
measurement and accountability  
in translating ambition into  
tangible impact.

CONTEXT 

STRENGTH
THROUGH UNITY

FOOTBALL NEEDS TO ACCELERATE
In a context of increased stakeholder 
expectations, UEFA and European 
football are not only embracing this  
call to action but also accelerating  
their response. The mobilising power  
of the sport will help in making a  
positive and credible contribution 
to a sustainable future for the next 
generations of football players and  
fans, at international, national and  
local levels – with initiatives positively 
impacting communities and civil society.

UNITED FOR SUCCESS
The sustainability agenda is firmly 
embedded in UEFA’s strategic vision 
for 2024–30, United for Success, with 
one of the five strategic pillar anchored 
around these topics. This reflects the 
organisation’s desire to ensure that  
all stakeholders trust and engage  
with football, and that the sport 
is responsible.

IT’S ABOUT FOOTBALL  
AND SUSTAINABILITY
Our societies are facing social and 
environmental challenges. As an intrinsic 
part of these communities, UEFA feels 
the obligation to address these concerns 
in close cooperation with its European 
football stakeholders. 

This includes socially responsible and 
environmentally friendly practices, which 
are addressed in this strategy under the 
term sustainability, in close alignment 
with international standards. 

Acknowledging the relevance of 
sustainability can benefit football while 
inspiring and mobilising the wider 
society. This requires a shared vision 
and collaborative actions toward a set 
of objectives to mobilise the expansive 
football fan community and create 
strong impacts.

DRIVING CHANGE TOGETHER
The rising awareness of environmental 
and societal priorities needs to turn 
into concrete action, with a particular 
focus on achieving tangible results. 
The scale of our challenges calls for 
coordinated, joint action by multiple 
players and constant adaptation. No 
one acting in isolation can hope to find 
the necessary answers and ensure 
their implementation. It’s going to take 
teamwork with our stakeholders!

FUNDAMENTALS AND 
GUIDING PRINCIPLES 

CORE CONVICTIONS

FUNDAMENTALS
UEFA’s approach is grounded in a set of unchanging, fundamental convictions that 
guide the Football Sustainability Strategy and its implementation.

WE FOCUS ON FOOTBALL AND 
ITS IMPACT ON SOCIETY
We prioritise issues that are relevant for 
European football, working with partners 
and institutions based on mutual 
convictions and trust, using our voices 
to raise awareness about the issues 
that matter. 

WE BELIEVE SUSTAINABILITY 
SUPPORTS THE SUCCESS OF 
EUROPEAN FOOTBALL
We underscore the importance of 
managing sustainability in UEFA’s core 
activities as an investment in football’s 
future prosperity. As part of this, we 
actively pursue opportunities with host 
cities, partners and other stakeholders 
to source, experiment and roll out 
product and service innovations.

WE ADVOCATE RESPECT FOR HUMAN 
RIGHTS AND THE ENVIRONMENT
We are committed to respecting, 
protecting and promoting human 
rights through a comprehensive set of 

measures designed to ensure the welfare 
and safety of all engaged in football. 
On the environmental front, we focus 
on reducing our environmental footprint 
through targeted investments in key 
areas material to football.

WE ACT IN LINE WITH 
TRANSPARENT, LONG-TERM 
OBJECTIVES
We commit to a long-term plan up  
to 2030, communicating on progress 
year-by-year. 

This lays the ground for a trust-based 
dialogue and collaboration with all 
stakeholders.

WE WORK AS ONE TEAM, 
WITH ONE COMMON LANGUAGE 
AND APPROACH
We work in synergy with all to amplify 
football’s positive impact and make the 
most of our collective efforts, rallying 
around a common language and 
approach. 

14 UEFA Football Sustainability Strategy

15

 GUIDING PRINCIPLES
This actionable UEFA strategy is made available to all football stakeholders to inspire 
and support them in formulating their own sustainability approaches.

APPROACH
The strategy is formulated around 
11 policies, each supported by a 
2030 ambition, targets and key 
performance indicators (KPIs), and will 
be implemented in five areas of action. 
The issues covered by the policies are 
interconnected. 

AGILITY
UEFA’s approach is expected to 
evolve through periodical reviews and 
assessments of progress. This may lead 
to consolidating some of the policies. 

Given the dynamic nature of 
sustainability, an integrated and flexible 
method is essential to tackle social 
and environmental considerations and 
balance them all. 

ESG 
Environmental, social and governance 
(ESG) standards and mechanisms are 
embedded to ensure the alignment of 
sustainability objectives with operational 
practices and financing strategies.  

RISK MANAGEMENT  
UEFA’s enterprise risk management 
system identifies sustainability risks and 
formulates mitigation actions covering 

financial, operational, reputational and 
strategic dimensions.  

CONFORMITY 
The strategy aligns with UEFA’s statutes, 
strategy, regulations and guidelines. 

It also concurs with internationally 
recognised frameworks and standards, 
including, among others, the UN 
Sustainable Development Goals, the UN 
Sports for Climate Action Framework, 
the European Green Deal, the Universal 
Declaration of Human Rights, the UN 
Guiding Principles on Business and 
Human Rights, and the UN Global 
Compact Principles.

REPORTING
Each season, our performance against 
the targets set in this strategy is 
consolidated in the UEFA Respect 
Report, with a view to ensuring 
transparency and accountability.

OVERSIGHT
The strategy and its implementation 
are overseen by the UEFA Executive 
Committee and the UEFA Social and 
Environmental Sustainability (SES) 
Committee.

communicate their own sustainability approach.

 THE ROAD TO 2030 AND BEYOND

Following the commitment we made in 2021, we upgraded our sustainability 
strategy in the second half of 2025 after assessing its effectiveness and 
analysing the lessons learned from the targeted measures and investments 
undertaken over the past years.

2021-2025

Upgrade

2026-2030
and beyond

Throughout this process, which included stakeholder consultation (see Chapter 
5 below), we aimed to ensure that our strategic outlook remains relevant and 
impactful for European football, with a view to continuing to raise ambition, 
accelerate action and embed sustainability deeper into the game. 

In this context, it is important to underline that while this strategy is based 
around a 2030 end point, its ambition and actions have been designed to 
create lasting impact far beyond then.

 STAKEHOLDERS

collaboration is necessary to maximise positive impacts while

OUR FOOTBALL ECOSYSTEM:

UEFA aims to rally the European football 
ecosystem around a common agenda 
and create effective synergies. At 
the heart of European football, UEFA 
operates in tandem with its 55 member 
associations, while leagues and clubs 
play an active role in organising games 
and competitions. 

Other stakeholders actively participate 
in UEFA competitions at each level 
of the game, from players and fans 
to coaches, referees, officials and 

volunteers. Sponsors, the media and 
different institutions complete the 
stakeholder field. 

In undertaking collaborative efforts with 
its stakeholders, UEFA can leverage the 
heartfelt, shared passion for football to 
offer a platform for collaboration that 
unites participants around the positive 
values of the sport. This is underpinned 
by the popularity of football, which 
enables UEFA to amplify the message of 
sustainability to a global audience.

 STAKEHOLDER CONSULTATION

In October 2025, UEFA carried out a survey to assess stakeholder perceptions of 39 
topics across 11 policy areas. Stakeholders were asked to rate each topic from 1 (very 
low) to 5 (very good/high) across four dimensions: relevance (importance for UEFA’s 
sustainability agenda), impacts (effects on people and the environment), risks (potential 
operational, financial, reputational or regulatory consequences) and opportunities 
(potential benefits such as innovation, efficiency, partnerships, brand value and 
stakeholder trust).

Perceived risks are moderate across all policies, with no critical outliers. This indicates that 
stakeholders consider UEFA’s current approach robust, though social issues, particularly 
Anti-racism and Equality & Inclusion, are seen as areas in which operational or reputational 
risks may be more pronounced. At the same time, all policies are associated with high 
opportunity ratings, especially Football for All Abilities, Child & Youth Protection and Anti-
racism. 

Environmental themes also scored highly in opportunity perceptions, suggesting that 
stakeholders believe UEFA can create significant added value through innovation, 
community impact and leadership in sustainable event operations. Overall, the graphs 
reflect broad alignment, confirming that UEFA’s policy areas are well-positioned and  
widely supported, which provides a solid foundation for prioritisation in the next phase 
of the strategy.

POLICIES

SOCIAL IMPACT 

Football is all about people – a common passion that brings together 
individuals of different ages, backgrounds, nationalities and abilities. 
The divisions and discrimination that afflict our societies inevitably play 
out on and around the pitch, but the sport can be a powerful vehicle for 
challenging and overcoming them, generating positive impact in society. 

SOCIETY AND FOOTBALL
Everyone involved in football 
should be afforded dignity, 
inclusion, protection and equal 
rights and opportunities, in a spirit 
of freedom and justice. 

Football must be a community 
that welcomes everyone and offers 
them equal access and a safe 
and secure environment. Everyone 
should be able to be involved in 
football as their authentic self. 

The value that sport brings to both 
our physical and mental health 
should also be emphasised. 

OUR COMMITMENT TO ACT
In accordance with the UEFA 
Human Rights Commitment 
approved in 2021, we strive for 
an inclusive culture in which no 
one is discriminated against or 
excluded based on any personal 
traits – whether playing, coaching, 
refereeing or organising the game, 
and including all aspects of the 
game itself and any activities 
connected to it. In addition, UEFA 
aspires for football to be a driver 
for impact more broadly, engaging 
society and governments on key 
topics and providing information 
and education.

#FOOTBALL PROGRAMME 
These core beliefs are reflected in our #FootbAll programme, which spans the social 
policies and highlights the power of football to drive positive social change across 
Europe, advocating that the game is open to all to enjoy, play, learn and develop. 
The following seven policies have been identified for the strategic period of 
2026–30 and are explained in the following pages:

Environmental sustainability contributes to football’s long-term viability. 
The sport can play its part in addressing environmental challenges through 
targeted measures and investments.

its environmental impact and harness the power of football to catalyse solutions among 
organisations, host cities and fans. Progress is measured through efforts to prevent, 
reduce and remediate football’s environmental impact.

RESPONSIBLE MANAGEMENT

Responsible management reinforces football’s long-term resilience. 
By embedding strong ESG principles into the way UEFA designs venues and 
delivers competitions, the game can enhance operational quality, reduce 
risks and create long-lasting value for host communities.

OPERATIONS AND FOOTBALL
Football’s operational impact is 
inherently linked to the venues 
where the game takes place and 
to the way competitions of all 
scales are organised. 

The planning, construction and 
operation of venues influence 
accessibility, safety, efficiency

the delivery of competitions, 
from matchday logistics to 
stakeholder coordination, 
shapes football’s operational 
footprint. A unified ESG matrix 
applied across all UEFA events, 
not only flagship finals, ensures 

coherent expectations, clearer 
responsibilities and more 
accountable processes throughout 
the entire football calendar. 
UEFA can strengthen trust and 
performance by promoting 
transparent, measurable and  
high-quality operational 
standards.

for event delivery and supports

and elevate the legacy left by each

OUR COMMITMENT TO ACT
For the 2026–30 strategic period, UEFA focuses its operational responsibility around 
two core policies: event sustainability, emphasising structured ESG management 
systems, accountable delivery processes and clear criteria applicable to all UEFA 
events; and infrastructure sustainability, guiding the development, upgrading 
and operation of venues.

MOVING FORWARD

EXISTING INITIATIVES 

Creating the UEFA ESPES enabled the 
measurement and benchmarking of event 
sustainability in football and allows the 
social and environmental impact of football 
events to be traced from end to end. Moving 
forward, UEFA will collaborate closely with 
member associations, leagues and clubs 
to promote the UEFA ESPES and enable 
football stakeholders to apply it across 
various event scopes. In addition, an event 
sustainability manual will be created that 
consolidates all sustainability guidance for 
football stakeholders into one accessible and 
user-friendly resource. This will encourage 
continuous improvement, in turn leading to 
further cooperation and innovation with host 
cities, partners and other football stakeholders 
to shape a sustainable legacy for events.

THE WAY FORWARD  
TO 2030 AND BEYOND 

ACCELERATING ACTION

TURNING THE UEFA FOOTBALL SUSTAINABILITY STRATEGY INTO CONCRETE 
ACTION REQUIRES A WILLINGNESS TO ADAPT FROM ALL PARTIES INVOLVED.

Difficult trade-offs might have to be discussed and made concerning short term 
versus long term, profit versus purpose, risks versus opportunities and priority setting. 
The foundations have been laid and multiple guidelines, toolkits and frameworks have 
been produced across all the topical areas set out in this document. The next phase 
requires shifting towards solution-oriented implementation and measurable results, 
supported by targeted change management measures that enable consistent delivery 
across the football ecosystem. UEFA will accelerate the process by implementing the 
following priority steps:

 - Continuous investments via support systems, tools, guidelines and regulations

 - Refined action plans for each policy and area of action 

 - An ever-larger community of sustainability managers connected by a common 

process and common terminology  

 - Guidelines and support programmes for developing human resources, 

sustainability strategies and action plans at member associations and other 
football stakeholders  

 - Measuring and monitoring progress for annual reporting on actions and results, in 

alignment with international standards  

 - ESG (environmental, social and governance) criteria and datasets linking 

sustainability, operational and financing strategies 

 - An acknowledgement that the top-down approach advocated by UEFA for the 
European football pyramid will need to be complemented with a bottom-up 
approach with regard fans, communities and amateur clubs

This journey will continue to present challenges. To overcome these, the European 
football ecosystem must acknowledge the urgency for action and work towards a 
common agenda. As the future of football is close to all our hearts, UEFA calls upon 
the entire football community to play their part and engage in this platform. Strength 
through unity!

 TARGETS AND KEY 
PERFORMANCE INDICATORS

As shown in the following pages, for each of the 11 policies, topics have been broken 
down into targets and key performance indicators (KPIs) which guide the action plan. 
Recognising where we are today, we have developed aspirational and operational 
targets to demonstrate our commitment towards the long-term ambitions of our 11 
policies. Aspirational targets relating to seven specific policies represent the ultimate 
sustainable impacts to be achieved by UEFA within its organisation and with reference 
to its events, as well as collaboratively across European football. 

Operational targets represent the drivers of our aspirations and are related to the 
levers that UEFA can mobilise to inspire, activate and accelerate sustainable change. 
These operational targets are further qualified in terms of timing (short, medium and 
long term) and level of difficulty (increasing from 1 to 5). To ensure transparency and 
accountability, we have defined specific KPIs to continuously monitor our progress 
against both aspirational and operational targets. A link to specific sustainable 
development goals (SDGs) is also provided to integrate our targets with the SDG 
framework. As described in Chapter 4 under our guiding principles, each season, a 
reporting process outlining performance against targets is consolidated in the UEFA 
Respect Report.

ASPIRATIONAL TARGETS FOR 2030
 - ANTI-DISCRIMINATION: Eradicate discriminatory incidents across all UEFA events and advocate 

action across European football.

 - CHILD & YOUTH PROTECTION: Eradicate episodes of abuse at UEFA events and advocate action 

across European football.

 - EQUALITY, DIVERSITY AND INCLUSION: Ensure football is open, welcoming and accessible to 

 -

everyone by promoting equal opportunities on and off the pitch.
FOOTBALL FOR ALL ABILITIES: Guarantee barrier-free access for any individual wanting to play, 
attend events or work in football. 

 - CIRCULAR ECONOMY: Pursue a road to zero plastic waste and food waste within UEFA and across 

UEFA events, and advocate action across European football.

 - CLIMATE AND ADVOCACY: Accelerate action towards reducing greenhouse gas emissions by 50% 

within UEFA and across UEFA events, and advocate action across European football.

 - EVENT SUSTAINABILITY: Continuously improve each UEFA event’s sustainability performance level.
